levers.domain_notes: Sourcing: scholarly APIs first for eval/judge methodology (LLM-as-judge validity, agreement metrics, calibration); official docs via Context7/fetch for every selected library (retrieval, storage, LLM SDKs, eval harnesses); engineering sources for data pipeline and IR. Evidence norms: measured experiments outrank vendor claims; GitHub maintenance/issues outrank stars; recent (2024-2026) docs outrank old blog posts. Recency window 1-2 years, verified as of September 14, 2026.

scope_conditions: ONE brand only, chosen for submission quality not row count
Banking77 for intent work ONLY, never to inflate headline results
evaluators run a subsample, not the full 3M rows; subsample must be fast yet defensible
README must reproduce headline results in under 15 minutes
no technology anchoring: no forced LangChain/Pinecone/agents/vector-DB; simplest architecture that achieves quality wins
existing workspace implementation is untrusted input to be measured, not preserved
no fabricated numbers: unmeasured quantities reported as NOT MEASURED or ESTIMATED
sub_questions: What does good mean for the selected brand, and what was deliberately NOT built?
Which brand maximizes submission quality (volume, coverage, depth, intent diversity, resolution consistency, golden-set sufficiency, escalation opportunity)?
How must the Twitter conversation graph be reconstructed (tweet relations, inbound/outbound, multi-turn threads, noise, masking) without treating rows as independent?
How are train/test/golden splits built to prevent conversation, near-duplicate, temporal, response, and retrieval-contamination leakage (past-data to future-message)?

How is a small, mutually distinguishable, routable intent taxonomy derived from the brand data (clustering/embeddings/topic discovery + manual inspection), and what is Banking77 legitimately used for?
How is the golden set of 150-250 examples sampled (stratified by intent/difficulty/escalation/temporal + random + hard negatives), labelled, and documented without cherry-picking?
What do trivial (majority/fixed/always-escalate) and simple (TF-IDF/BM25, nearest-neighbor, direct-LLM) baselines score, and why are they honest rather than strawmen?

How are intent (accuracy, macro-F1, per-class PR, confusion), retrieval (relevance of problems/resolutions), reply (correctness, grounding, usefulness, brand fit, hallucination), and escalation (precision/recall, coverage-vs-quality) measured independently?
Which retrieval strategy (lexical vs dense vs hybrid + rerank + metadata/thread-aware filtering) retrieves similar problems with useful resolutions rather than similar wording, at what latency/cost?
Which LLM(s) serve which component (classification vs generation vs judging), with what prompts, structured outputs, confidence, fallbacks, and routing — and is any agent framework justified?
What escalation policy and calibrated threshold automate only safe cases, with stated reasons, and how does the coverage-vs-quality curve behave?
What is the LLM-as-judge rubric, and how well does it agree with humans (correlation/agreement/weighted agreement with disagreement analysis) — why should the judge be trusted?
What are the top 5 real failure modes (example, expected vs actual, root cause, mitigation, implemented or not)?
What is misleading about the headline number (imbalance, easy samples, leakage, judge bias, rare-intent gaps, unsafe auto-handles)?

Which data-engineering (pandas/Polars/DuckDB/Arrow/Parquet), storage (SQLite/DuckDB/Postgres-pgvector/FAISS/Chroma/LanceDB/ES/OpenSearch/managed), eval (RAGAS/DeepEval/LangSmith/Langfuse/Braintrust/promptfoo), observability, deployment, and testing choices survive evidence, and at what cost/latency/reliability?

How are reproducibility (15-minute headline repro, subsample design), security/privacy (PII/masking, prompt injection, secrets), performance (p50/p95, tokens, cost), and scalability (indexing, concurrency, API limits) guaranteed without over-engineering?
If the current workspace implementation were submitted as-is, what would reviewers criticize, and which highest-value changes erase those criticisms?
